title: FIDE announces call for candidates for Athletes Commission elections
summary: FIDE has opened the call for candidates for the upcoming elections to the FIDE Athletes Commission. The Athletes Commission represents the interests and perspectives of players within FIDE, helping ensure that their voices are heard in discussions and decisions that affect the chess community. The overall composition of the Athletes’ Commission will consist of between 5 and 9 members, including mandatory representation of both genders. The exact final number will be determined by the Council, taking into account: The number of applications submitted; and The candidates’ readiness to work on the relevant Commission. The upcoming elections will be for an interim two-year term, from 2026 to 2028. This transitional period will give FIDE and the newly elected Commission time to develop clear and comprehensive rules for how the Athletes Commission should operate and be composed in the future. FIDE’s intention is that, once this interim term concludes in 2028, future elections will be conducted by and among the players themselves, further strengthening the Commission’s role as a representative voice for athletes in chess. FIDE is committed to giving players a stronger role within the governance of the International Chess Federation and ensuring that their views are properly represented. “As players, we experience the sport from a very particular perspective. We know where things work well, but we also see where improvements can be made,” said FIDE Interim President Viswanathan Anand. “It is important that this experience has a clear voice within FIDE. I hope strong candidates will come forward who are ready to listen to their fellow players, bring their concerns and ideas to the table, and help us build a Commission that the chess community feels genuinely represents them,” he added.  Once elected, the new Athletes Commission will work with FIDE to develop concrete proposals for increasing player representation within FIDE’s structures and to help shape additional regulations governing the Commission. This work will focus on strengthening representation, protecting players’ rights, and supporting the integrity and continued development of chess. Elections timeline Deadline for submission of candidacies: 07 October 2026 Final list of verified candidates: will be published no later than 12 October 2026 Elections: will be conducted by the newly elected FIDE Council during the October 2026. Candidacy requirements To stand for election to the Athletes Commission, a candidate must: a) be at least 18 years old;b) have competed in at least one of the last three FIDE World Championship Cycles, open or Women’s (namely: World Cup, Grand Prix Series, Candidates Tournament, Grand Swiss), or have qualified for the next FIDE World Championship Cycles, open or Women’s (namely: World Cup, Grand Prix Series, Candidates Tournament, Grand Swiss);c) be able to speak and understand English reasonably well;d) not be under a FIDE EDC disqualification. Candidates do not need the endorsement of a Member Federation in order to apply. Submission of candidacies Applications should be submitted by email to office@fide.com. Players should include their full name and clearly state that they wish to stand as a candidate for membership of the FIDE Athletes Commission. FIDE will confirm receipt of each application in writing. Candidates are also encouraged, although not required, to include a short letter in their own words explaining why they would like to serve on the Commission and what they hope to contribute.

title: GCL 2026, Day 4: FYERS American Gambits go on top with win over PBG Alaskan Knights; Triveni Continental Kings upset overnight leaders Alpine APL Pipers
summary: The match between Ganges Grandmasters and PBG Alaskan Knights witnessed decisive outcomes on all six boards for the first time in the competition; FYERS American Gambits win first return match. FYERS American Gambits reclaimed the top spot in the Global Chess League (GCL), a joint initiative of Tech Mahindra and FIDE, in Bengaluru on Tuesday with a thumping win over PBG Alaskan Knights, benefiting from two-time champions Triveni Continental Kings’ upset win over table toppers Alpine APL Pipers. The Continental Kings, who were at the bottom of the standings with just one win from four matches, defeated the Pipers 10-4, while CheQ Mumba Masters got the better of FYERS American Gambits 11-6 in the fifth-round matches. In the most dramatic match of the tournament so far, Ganges Grandmasters defeated PBG Alaskan Knights 12-8, with all six boards ending decisively. The Alaskan Knights also lost their second match of the day, going down 12-9 against FYERS American Gambits, as all six boards produced a result for the second time in a day. Let’s take a closer look at today’s action: Ganges Grandmasters vs. PBG Alaskan Knights: 12-8 The opening match of the day between Ganges Grandmasters, who are now third in the standings with nine match points, and PBG Alaskan Knights set the tone for a sensational day 4 at the GCL. While it was the first match in which all six boards produced decisive outcomes, a drama on the Prodigy board ultimately became the biggest talking point of the day. On the icon board, Ian Nepomniachtchi dispatched Viswanathan Anand in just 23 moves, while Polina Shuvalova registered her third win in four games by beating Kateryna Lagno. The Player of the Match Leinier Dominguez Perez squeezed out a win over 15-year-old Yagiz Kaan Erdogmus, who cracked under time pressure. But it looked like those three victories would not really help the Ganges Grandmasters wrap up the match as Arjun Erigaisi beat Levon Aronian and Nino Batsiashvili got the better of Stavroula Tsolakidou to close the gap to one point while Abhimanyu Mishra had a clearly winning position on the Prodigy board, although both players were in severe time trouble. The match score read 9-8 in favour of the Ganges Grandmasters, playing white, but they were clearly staring down the barrel. With just a second left on the clock, Mishra did not legally complete the move while promoting his pawn to a queen as the pieces were not in the right position when he hit the clock. Mendonca was quick to bring it to the notice of the arbiter and ended up winning the game on time and Ganges Grandmasters clinched the match. Explaining the reasoning behind his choice, Mendonca said, “He wanted to take my rook and make a queen. He pressed the clock and he went from  to three seconds. I was given one minute but it had to be made one second for him.” “He was clearly winning and I knew this was my only chance. I have had this discussion with a friend about how much time it takes to win a piece and convert it into a queen in a second. And I knew it was very difficult,” Mendonca added. Mishra was understandably gutted. “It really hurts because if I had won, my team would have won the match,” he said, while explaining how things unfolded. CheQ Mumba Masters vs. FYERS American Gambits: 11-6 CheQ Mumba Masters caught up with the Pipers in the standings as Shakhriyar Mamedyarov defeated Daniil Dubov in 42 moves, while Carissa Yip took full advantage of Sara Khadem’s misstep in an equal endgame to make it two wins for her team. M Pranesh had a chance to extend that lead further as he was in driver’s seat against Nihal Sarin but blundered a checkmate in one move. Still, Mamedyarov’s and Yip’s victories were enough for the Mumba Masters to clinch the match. Alpine APL Pipers vs. Triveni Continental Kings: 4-10 In the third match of the day, table toppers Alpine APL Pipers had the opportunity to extend their lead as they faced the Continental Kings, who didn’t have the best of starts to the competition. However, the match followed a somewhat unexpected script. With four games drawn, Aravindh Chithambaram defeated Vidit Gujrathi in a topsy-turvy battle, while Pranav V forced Volodar Murzin to resign after 63 moves to secure the win for their team. FYERS American Gambits vs. PBG Alaskan Knights: 12-9 In the last match of the day, all six games ended decisively as well, with the Gambits wrapping it up thanks to three victories with the black pies. However, the scoreline and the match result could have been completely different. Arjun Erigaisi reached a winning position against Nihal Sarin in a tricky ending, but first missed a win and then even a draw. At the end of day 4, FYERS American Gambits had taken the top spot in the standings with three match wins and 52 game points but had played one match more than their nearest challengers. Defending champions Alpine APL Pipers and CheQ Mumba Masters have nine match points and 47 game points each and are currently in second and third positions, respectively. The league brings together leading chess players from across the globe in a unique joint team format, with six players representing each franchise across Icons, Superstar Men, Superstar Women and Prodigies.
